inputs.original_text:
This ruling from the Punjab and Haryana High Court, with Justice Sumeet Goel, makes it clear that anticipatory bail can't be yanked just because stolen articles weren't recovered or the accusations come across as serious. There has to be actual evidence of someone abusing their freedom or some new development before any cancellation happens. They rejected the attempt to cancel the pre-arrest bail in this house case.

What stands out here is how this directly confronts a justice system that relies on unproven claims and scare tactics to strip away basic freedoms from the most vulnerable among us. It exposes how these loose standards lock in inequality, letting institutions target working people and marginalized communities with little real accountability. We need urgent, deeper reforms to protect rights and dismantle the structural discrimination that keeps these oppressive patterns alive.
